item.title: Undertone 1.38.3
item.description:
• Answer cards in job interviews. What you tell Ask about a meeting (job description, company, your résumé) now feeds the answer cards during the call. An interview on a personal calendar gets cards too, drawn only from what you told Ask, never from work tools or other workspaces.
  • Interview answers from your own background. For "tell me about a time…", "how would you…" or "introduce yourself", cards suggest an example from your résumé and how it fits the role.

Undertone 1.38.2

  • Faster web search:** looking something up on the web now takes about 6–10 seconds instead of 12–17, so it fits inside answers during a call. Each site shows up once in the sources list.

Undertone 1.38.1

  • Prep starts from what you told Ask. Emails, job descriptions, notes and files you give Ask are now kept, and Prep, "prep me for…" requests and automatic briefings for the same company or people use them first, even from an earlier conversation.
  • No unrelated topics in a prep. Past meetings are matched by the company and people on the invite, not by words like "meetings" or "tasks", and briefs leave out work that isn't about the meeting.
  • Workspaces stay apart in amem. Each workspace now has its own amem memory, so one workspace's recaps don't show up in another's answers.
  • Long messages you paste into Ask stay whole for the rest of the conversation.

Undertone 1.38.0

  • Search the web (Sources › Public web): when your own sources don't have the answer, or you ask it to research something online (a company, a product, someone's public role, news), Undertone can look it up on the public internet with your AI's built-in search. Works in Ask, answers during calls and research. Your sources are always searched first, answers say which facts came from the web with links, and only the search words are sent. Off until you turn it on.

Undertone 1.37.4

  • A question taken for someone else's turn now gets its card after all if you start answering it within 30 seconds (for example "what is your order of execution here?" asked without your name).
  • Questions about what you're working on, prioritizing, your roadmap or timeline are no longer mistaken for just handing someone the floor.
